chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Rifah ibn Musa said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), saying: 'I buy a slave-girl and she stays with me for months without menstruating, and this is not due to old age.' I said: 'And I show her to the women and they say she is not pregnant.' 'Is it permissible for me to have intercourse with her in her private part?' He said: 'He said: Indeed, wind can prevent menstruation without pregnancy, so there is no harm in having intercourse with her in her private part.'

I said: 'And if it is pregnancy, what is mine from her if I wish?' He said: 'You have what is below the private part until she completes four months and ten days of pregnancy. When her pregnancy exceeds four months and ten days, there is no harm in marrying her in the private part.'

I said: 'Al-Mughirah and his companions say it is not proper for a man to have intercourse with his wife while she is pregnant and her pregnancy has become evident, until she gives birth and nurses her child.' He said: 'This is from the practices of the Jews.'

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشَرَةُ أَيَّامٍ: Four months and ten days (a specific period in pregnancy)
key_terms.اَلرِّيحُ: Wind (gas), used here as a cause of delayed menstruation
key_terms.اَلْمُغِيرَةُ: Al-Mughirah ibn Sa'id, a prominent Shia jurist

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on having intercourse with a pregnant wife or slave in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Musa ibn Ja'far?
ai.summary: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) establishes that sexual intercourse with a pregnant female slave is permissible throughout pregnancy, distinguishing this from the view of Al-Mughirah who prohibited it after pregnancy became evident, a stance the Imam attributes to Jewish custom. The ruling specifies that while the master retains rights to the body until the fourth month and ten days (a period associated with the soul's entry or significant fetal development), the prohibition is not absolute but rather a matter of scholarly difference rooted in external influences.
